applies_why: The judge text makes Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because it admits two readings, which is the rule's forbidden treatment of a two-sense verse as open.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: the phrase 'carries two senses at once is not open': one reading allows UNDERDETERMINED when a verse admits two readings; the other says the verse is not open and both senses stand
why: Because the judge's UNDERDETERMINED verdict rests on Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings, it treats a two-sense verse as open contrary to K-S2.
